subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should OpenClaw standardize Skill Workshop lifecycle invariants as a core docs/tests contract, an optional AISP/AISOP reference package, a ClawHub package, or no new artifact?
rationale: The request formalizes security-sensitive Skill Workshop behavior and could create a new authority over scanner, apply, rollback, target, and surface-consistency rules, so automation should not choose the contract format or repository home.

options.title: OpenClaw-native contract first
options.body: Add a narrow docs/test fixture that mirrors current Skill Workshop invariants without introducing an AISP runtime dependency, then revisit AISP packaging later.

options.title: Reference package outside core
options.body: Ask the contributor to publish the AISP/AISOP package as a ClawHub or external reference artifact while OpenClaw keeps source and docs as authority.

options.title: Decline new contract artifact
options.body: Keep the current service, docs, and tests as the only Skill Workshop lifecycle authority and close the proposal after maintainer confirmation.

recommendation.title: OpenClaw-native contract first
recommendation.body: Add a narrow docs/test fixture that mirrors current Skill Workshop invariants without introducing an AISP runtime dependency, then revisit AISP packaging later.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history evidence points to this person as the central Skill Workshop proposal store introducer.
